user.title: Genbu Assistant
user.description: Genbu keeps your Genbu Shows on one version, the house version. It starts where your newest Show is, and the Genbu Show firmware card on the Genbu Assistant device offers the next one. Shows found: {count}.

abort.already_configured: Genbu Assistant is set up already
abort.single_instance_allowed: Genbu Assistant is set up already

init.title: Genbu Assistant
init.description: The house's update card, its release channel and the night install are on the Genbu Assistant device.

data_description.searxng_url: The address of your SearXNG, like http://10.0.0.5:8080. With it, a Genbu Show can look up a recipe and put it on its screen when asked (its Recipes switch). Empty: no recipes.
data_description.conversation_agent: The agent that answers on a Show, like an Ollama or OpenAI one. Genbu Assistant then is a conversation agent too: picked in an Assist pipeline instead of that agent, it answers a lone word the speech-to-text made of the TV with "I didn't catch that." and hands everything else on to it. Empty: no agent of Genbu's own.

error.searxng: That is no http or https address.
error.own_agent: That is Genbu Assistant's own agent; pick the one it should hand on to.

forget_show.name: Forget a Show
forget_show.description: Forgets a Show that has left the house for good: its versions, its music choice and its switches are dropped. The installer's --remove-show calls this after the Show is out of ESPHome.

node.name: Node name
node.description: The Show's ESPHome node name, as in shows on the house version sensor.

install_updates.name: Install updates on every Show
install_updates.description: When the Genbu Show firmware card has an update waiting, the house installs it and every Show follows. Otherwise each Show that is behind with an update of its own installs that. A Show calls this when somebody says yes to an update; the voice kit's "install the updates" calls it too.

except_node.name: Except node
except_node.description: The ESPHome node name of a Show to leave out, because it is installing already.

music_route.name: Where music plays
music_route.description: What the voice kit asks before it plays music: where music asked for on a Show plays right now, which speakers were passed over because they are off, and whether the Show should mention them (the first time, then at most once an hour).

show.name: Show
show.description: The Show's device or its voice satellite.

player.name: Speaker
player.description: A speaker somebody named. When it is off, nothing plays and the Show itself is offered instead.

show_key.name: Give a Show a new key
show_key.description: Admins only. Makes a new Home Assistant key for the Show's user, and a user first if it has none (no admin, home only), and hands the key to the Show over its encrypted ESPHome connection. The user's old keys are deleted once the Show has stored the new one. The installer calls this.

url.name: Home Assistant address
url.description: Where the Show finds Home Assistant from now on, inside your home. Leave it empty to keep the one it has.

key_gone.title: {show} lost its key to Home Assistant
key_gone.description: Home Assistant turned {show} away: the key it signs in with was deleted. That happens when someone deletes it under the user {user}, or switches that user off for a while, which deletes its keys too. If {show} was lost or stolen, leave this alone: that is the lock doing its job. Otherwise Genbu can give it a new key.

confirm.title: Give {show} a new key
confirm.description: Genbu makes a new key for {show}'s user, hands it to {show} over its encrypted ESPHome connection, and deletes the user's old keys once {show} has stored the new one. Only do this for a Show that is in your home.

abort.no_show: This Show is not in ESPHome right now.
abort.still_away: The Show was turned away again. Check how it reaches Home Assistant first.
abort.no_answer: The Show did not answer. Is it on and connected?
abort.not_stored: The Show did not store the new key. Nothing changed: the new key was deleted again.
abort.not_encrypted: The Show's ESPHome connection has no encryption key, and a key only goes over an encrypted one. Run the installer for it again.
abort.user_off: The Show's user is switched off. Switch it on in Settings → People first.
abort.not_a_show_user: The Show's user is an admin or may sign in from outside your home. A Show's user may neither.
abort.no_provider: Home Assistant has no sign-in with usernames to make the Show's user with.
abort.name_taken: Both sign-in names for the Show's user belong to someone else.

no_user.title: {show} has no user in Home Assistant
no_user.description: Home Assistant turned {show} away, and the user it signed in as is gone. If {show} was lost or stolen, leave this alone. Otherwise Genbu can make it a user again, the way the installer does, and give it a key.

confirm.title: Make {show} a user
confirm.description: Genbu makes a user for {show} that is no admin and may only sign in from home, gives it a key, and hands that to {show} over its encrypted ESPHome connection. Only do this for a Show that is in your home.

abort.no_show: This Show is not in ESPHome right now.
abort.still_away: The Show was turned away again. Check how it reaches Home Assistant first.
abort.no_answer: The Show did not answer. Is it on and connected?
abort.not_stored: The Show did not store the new key. Nothing changed: the new key was deleted again.
abort.not_encrypted: The Show's ESPHome connection has no encryption key, and a key only goes over an encrypted one. Run the installer for it again.
abort.user_off: The Show's user is switched off. Switch it on in Settings → People first.
abort.not_a_show_user: The Show's user is an admin or may sign in from outside your home. A Show's user may neither.
abort.no_provider: Home Assistant has no sign-in with usernames to make the Show's user with.
abort.name_taken: Both sign-in names for the Show's user belong to someone else.

user_off.title: {show}'s user is switched off
user_off.description: Home Assistant turned {show} away because its user, {user}, is switched off. Switching a user off deletes its keys as well. To let {show} back in, switch {user} on in Settings → People. Genbu then offers to give {show} a new key here.

not_a_show_user.title: {show} signs in as a user it should not
not_a_show_user.description: Home Assistant turned {show} away, and the user it signs in as, {user}, is an admin or may sign in from outside your home. A Show's key opens your whole home, so Genbu gives no key to a user like that. Make {user} a plain user that can only sign in from home in Settings → People, or run the installer for {show} again.

not_encrypted.title: {show}'s ESPHome connection is not encrypted
not_encrypted.description: Home Assistant turned {show} away. Genbu could give it a new key, but only over an encrypted connection, and {show}'s ESPHome connection has no encryption key. Run the installer for {show} again: it sets one up.

home_only.title: {show} comes in from outside your home
home_only.description: {show}'s user may only sign in from your home network, and Home Assistant saw {show} come from outside it. Usually something on the way hides where it comes from: a VPN that rewrites addresses (a Tailscale subnet router keeps them with --snat-subnet-routes=false), a reverse proxy Home Assistant does not trust (trusted_proxies), or a Home Assistant Cloud address. Fix the way in, not the user: a Show's user stays home only. Then have {show} try again here.

confirm.title: Have {show} try again
confirm.description: {show} signs in once more with the key it has. Do this after fixing how it reaches Home Assistant.
